title: Local acyclicity extends to locally constant prime-to-characteristic torsion sheaves
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally acyclic [def-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-abelian-sheaf]. Let $G$ be a locally constant abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] [def-constructible-locally-constant]. Suppose that, at every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, the group $G_{\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is torsion and every element has finite order prime to the characteristic of the residue field at $\bar x$ (any finite order is allowed in characteristic zero). Then $f$ is locally acyclic relative to $G$ [def-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-abelian-sheaf]. The stalk groups need not be finite and no single integer annihilating all stalks is required.

proof.text: Fix geometric x and t and write M=G_x and V for the strict-local fibre. The strict-local schemes are affine spectra. Their fibre product V is affine by the Mathlib pullback instance, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

Apply the germ-compatible constant comparison to each admissible constant cyclic sheaf on X. The point-fibre constant-sheaf isomorphism identifies its stalk with its coefficient group. Local acyclicity gives invertibility of its alpha and positive cohomology vanishing. Cancel the sections of the comparison and transport the constant-section unit by naturality along the stalk isomorphism. This proves the cyclic hypotheses of the constant-coefficient lemma on V, with p=char(k(x)). Transport the positive vanishing along the same sheaf isomorphisms. The Lean proof uses the general site-point sheafFiberConstantSheafIso implementation of the constant-stalk identification; only the isomorphism itself is needed here.
Use the coefficient devissage lemma on M with exactly the stalkwise torsion and coprimality assumption hG at x. It gives the constant-section isomorphism for M and positive vanishing on V.

Apply the germ-compatible comparison to G itself. Its stated equality identifies the canonical alpha with the constant-section isomorphism followed by sections of a sheaf isomorphism, so alpha is invertible. Positive vanishing transports along the sheaf isomorphism through singleFunctor and cohomology. Since x and t were arbitrary, this is precisely local acyclicity relative to G.
